title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the Status of Judicial Protection of Intellectual Property Rights by Chinese Courts (2009)
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Issuing the Report on Judicial Protection of Intellectual Property Rights by Chinese Courts (2009)

Fa [2010] No. 176

To: the High People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

To actively carry out the 2010 National Intellectual Property Publicity Week activities, deeply implement the National Intellectual Property Strategy, further strengthen the publicity of judicial protection of intellectual property rights, fully demonstrate the achievements of the People's Courts in the judicial protection of intellectual property rights, and strive to create a favorable atmosphere conducive to the healthy development of the judicial protection of intellectual property rights by the People's Courts, our Court has decided to issue the Report on Judicial Protection of Intellectual Property Rights by Chinese Courts (2009).

The Report on Judicial Protection of Intellectual Property Rights by Chinese Courts (2009) comprehensively reviews and summarizes the work of the People's Courts in judicial protection of intellectual property rights in 2009, and also provides a brief introduction to the work of judicial protection of intellectual property rights since the reform and opening up thirty years ago. It fully demonstrates the achievements made in China's judicial protection of intellectual property rights and highlights China's determination and confidence in protecting intellectual property rights. This is the first time the People's Courts have publicly introduced the judicial protection of intellectual property rights to society in the form of an annual protection report. It is an important measure for the People's Courts to further strengthen the judicial protection of intellectual property rights, a major event in the intellectual property adjudication work of the People's Courts, and one of the highlights of this year's work of the People's Courts. People's Courts at all levels should take this as an opportunity to further enhance their understanding of the importance and urgency of strengthening intellectual property adjudication work from the perspective of serving the overall work of the Party and the state, from the perspective of deeply implementing the National Intellectual Property Strategy, and from the perspective of promoting the construction of an innovative country, effectively play the dominant role of judicial protection of intellectual property rights, strengthen confidence, forge ahead with determination, be pioneering and innovative, work solidly, and strive to continuously open up new prospects for the judicial protection of intellectual property rights work.

Hereby notified.

April 16, 2010

**Report on Judicial Protection of Intellectual Property Rights by Chinese Courts (2009)**

**Foreword**

The People's Courts are the adjudicative organs of the state. In accordance with the Constitution and laws, they independently exercise adjudicative power and fulfill the sacred duty of judicial protection of intellectual property rights.

Accompanying the pace of China's reform and opening up, since the start of China's intellectual property rights cause in the late 1970s and early 1980s, under the high attention of the Party and the state, with the strong support of the whole society, and through the joint efforts of the vast number of judges in the People's Courts, the judicial protection of intellectual property rights by Chinese courts has grown from nothing, from weak to strong, and has continuously developed. Gradually, a socialist intellectual property judicial protection system with Chinese characteristics has been established, which can basically meet the needs of national development and fulfill the obligations of international treaties, becoming an important part of China's judicial cause.

- Over the past three decades, the function of the People's Courts in judicial protection of intellectual property rights has been continuously strengthened. The People's Courts provide comprehensive judicial protection for intellectual property rights by exercising three types of adjudicative functions: civil, administrative, and criminal. In civil adjudication, starting from the late 1970s with the trial of technology contract cases, in the mid-1980s successively beginning the trial of trademark, patent, and copyright civil cases, and in the early 1990s beginning the trial of unfair competition cases, the People's Courts have lawfully accepted and concluded a large number of intellectual property civil cases. From 1985 to 2009, the People's Courts concluded a total of 166,408 first-instance civil intellectual property cases. In administrative adjudication, since the implementation of the Patent Law in 1985 when the People's Courts began to accept patent administrative cases with the Patent Reexamination Board as the defendant, the relevant courts have earnestly fulfilled their judicial review responsibilities concerning cases involving the grant and confirmation of rights such as patents and trademarks, as well as cases of administrative enforcement of intellectual property laws. From 1985 to 2009, local courts nationwide concluded a total of 6,387 first-instance administrative intellectual property cases. In criminal adjudication, after the promulgation and implementation of the Criminal Law in 1979, the People's Courts provided criminal judicial protection for registered trademarks accordingly. After the revision of the Criminal Law in 1997, they provided comprehensive criminal judicial protection for various types of intellectual property rights, continuously increased the intensity of criminal judicial protection of intellectual property rights, and severely punished serious intellectual property crimes such as counterfeiting and piracy in accordance with the law. After the Supreme People's Court and the Supreme People's Procuratorate jointly issued a judicial interpretation on handling criminal cases of intellectual property infringement at the end of 2004, the number of criminal cases involving intellectual property infringement accepted and concluded by the People's Courts increased significantly. From 1997 to 2009, a total of 14,509 first-instance criminal intellectual property cases were concluded.

- Over the past three decades, the scope of judicial protection of intellectual property rights by the People's Courts has continuously expanded. Before the mid-1990s, the intellectual property cases accepted by the People's Courts were mainly technology contract cases. From the mid-1990s to 2002, patent cases were the most numerous. Since 2002, copyright cases have risen to first place. While the number of traditional copyright, patent, trademark, unfair competition, and technology contract cases continues to grow rapidly overall, judicial protection of intellectual property rights has continuously expanded into entirely new fields, including network copyrights, computer software copyrights, new plant varieties, integrated circuit layout designs, folk literature and art, geographical indications, special marks, enterprise names, domain names, judicial recognition of well-known trademarks, intangible cultural heritage, franchising, applications for pre-litigation interim measures, confirmation of non-infringement, and antitrust. In particular, cases involving network copyrights have increased rapidly in recent years. Currently, the cases accepted by the People's Courts cover all types of intellectual property rights and various forms of market competition behavior, involving the entire process of creation, utilization, protection, and management of intellectual property rights. Adjudication is increasingly becoming the main channel for parties to resolve intellectual property disputes. Taking patent protection as an example, the majority of rights holders choose to file civil lawsuits directly with the People's Courts to resolve disputes.

- Over the past three decades, the level of judicial protection of intellectual property rights by the People's Courts has continuously improved. The quality and efficiency of the People's Courts' adjudication of intellectual property cases have been continuously enhanced. The first-instance conclusion rate for intellectual property civil cases rose from 75.35% in 2003 to 85.35% in 2009. The appeal rate fell from 59.38% in 2003 to 48.82% in 2009. The rate of reversal or remand for retrial in second instance fell from 15.19% in 2003 to 6.00% in 2009. The retrial rate fell from 0.80% in 2003 to 0.33% in 2009. The effectiveness of mediation in litigation has been significant. In recent years, the average rate of mediation or withdrawal of lawsuits in first-instance intellectual property civil cases nationwide has consistently remained above 50%. In the adjudication of foreign-related intellectual property cases, the People's Courts adhere to the principle of equal legal protection, equally protect the legitimate rights and interests of Chinese and foreign parties in accordance with the law, and have established a good international judicial image. The transparency of judicial protection has continuously strengthened. The People's Courts consistently adhere to the principle of open trial, promptly publicizing effective judgments and adjudication information to society through media, the internet, publications, and other means in accordance with the law. On March 10, 2006, the Supreme People's Court officially launched the "China Intellectual Property Judgment Documents Website", uniformly publishing effective intellectual property judgment documents of People's Courts at all levels online.

- Over the past three decades, the intensity of judicial protection of intellectual property rights by the People's Courts has continuously increased. The People's Courts strictly order infringers to bear liability for infringement in accordance with the law, striving to reduce the cost of rights enforcement and increase the cost of infringement. When infringement is found to be established, the infringer is generally ordered to immediately cease the infringement. At the same time, the court ensures that the rights holder obtains sufficient damages, and appropriately alleviates the rights holder's burden of proof for damages in accordance with the law. For example, in the case of Wuhan Jingyuan Environmental Protection Engineering Co., Ltd. v. Japan Fujikasui Kogyo Co., Ltd. and Huayang Electric Power Co., Ltd. concerning infringement of invention patent rights, finally adjudicated by the Supreme People's Court at the end of 2009, the two defendants were ordered to jointly compensate the plaintiff for economic losses amounting to RMB 50,612,400 (approximately USD 7.42 million). This is currently the highest damages awarded in an intellectual property case adjudicated by the Supreme People's Court. The People's Courts actively, prudently, effectively, and reasonably adopt pre-litigation interim measures, and pay attention to applying civil sanctions to punish infringers in accordance with the law. From 2002 to 2009, local courts nationwide accepted a total of 808 applications for pre-litigation injunctions related to intellectual property rights, with an order support rate of 84.18%; accepted 1,312 applications for pre-litigation evidence preservation, with an order support rate of 93.72%; accepted 527 applications for pre-litigation property preservation, with an order support rate of 96.04%. The People's Courts particularly emphasize the role of criminal sanctions in protecting intellectual property rights. While lawfully applying principal penalties and standardizing the application of probation, they strengthen the application and enforcement of fines, actively take measures such as recovering illegal gains, confiscating criminal tools, destroying infringing products, and ordering compensation for losses, thereby depriving the infringer of the ability and conditions to re-offend economically.

- Over the past three decades, the judicial protection system for intellectual property rights by the People's Courts has continuously improved. Since 1985, the Supreme People's Court has formulated a total of 41 judicial interpretations on intellectual property rights, of which 29 are currently in effect; it has issued more than 40 judicial guiding documents with general guiding significance. Particularly since 2000, in response to the needs of WTO accession and building an innovative country, the Supreme People's Court has further intensified its judicial interpretation efforts, formulating 25 judicial interpretations on intellectual property rights. The promulgation and implementation of these judicial interpretations and guiding documents have provided more specific and clear bases for the People's Courts in both procedural and substantive aspects of adjudicating intellectual property cases, making the intellectual property adjudication system more comprehensive. The jurisdiction system for intellectual property cases has continuously improved. To ensure the trial quality of intellectual property cases, while designated jurisdiction has been applied to cases involving patents, new plant varieties, and integrated circuit layout designs from the outset, jurisdiction over other first-instance civil intellectual property cases has also been basically centralized in intermediate people's courts since 1998. In recent years, in response to the sharp increase in general intellectual property cases involving copyrights and trademarks, there has been active exploration in designating some basic people's courts to adjudicate general civil intellectual property cases. The causes of action for intellectual property cases have become more scientific and comprehensive. In April 2008, the Supreme People's Court promulgated and implemented the new Provisions on Causes of Action in Civil Cases, further concentrating and standardizing the causes of action in civil cases related to intellectual property and competition law. The allocation of adjudicative resources for intellectual property has continuously optimized. In the 1980s, civil cases on copyright and industrial property rights were handled by the civil adjudication tribunals and economic adjudication tribunals of the People's Courts respectively. From the 1990s onwards, these were gradually unified under specialized adjudication tribunals. In recent years, some local courts have also piloted the unified acceptance of civil, administrative, and criminal intellectual property cases by an intellectual property adjudication tribunal, and have explored the use of expanded collegial panels or the participation of civil judges in the adjudication of intellectual property criminal and administrative cases.

- Over the past three decades, the judicial protection capability of the People's Courts for intellectual property rights has continuously strengthened. The intellectual property adjudication organization of the People's Courts has continuously improved, team building has continuously strengthened, and the level of specialization has continuously increased. In August 1993, the Beijing High People's Court and the Beijing Intermediate People's Court were the first in the country to establish specialized intellectual property adjudication tribunals. The Supreme People's Court also established an intellectual property adjudication tribunal in October 1996. Currently, all high people's courts, most intermediate people's courts, and all basic people's courts with jurisdiction over civil intellectual property cases have established specialized intellectual property adjudication tribunals. According to statistics as of October 2008, there were 298 stand-alone intellectual property tribunals and 84 specialized intellectual property collegial panels in local courts nationwide, with a total of 2,126 judges engaged in intellectual property adjudication (as of now, there are a total of 31 high people's courts, 409 intermediate people's courts, and 3,119 basic people's courts in local ordinary courts nationwide). People's Courts generally select highly qualified and experienced judges for intellectual property adjudication; attach importance to the training of intellectual property judges and the intensive training of professional knowledge and adjudication skills; the judicial ability and professional level of intellectual property judges continuously improve; emphasis is placed on investigation and research and adherence to theoretical innovation; persistence in learning and research has become a common pursuit and professional characteristic of intellectual property judges.

In 2009, as the People's Republic of China traversed sixty years of trials and tribulations and achieved remarkable accomplishments admired by the world, the judicial protection of intellectual property rights by the People's Courts also achieved new progress. The People's Courts always adhere to the guidance of Deng Xiaoping Theory and the important thought of "Three Represents", deeply implement the Scientific Outlook on Development, closely focus on the overall work of the Party and the state, comprehensively implement the National Intellectual Property Strategy, attach importance to studying new situations and new issues facing intellectual property adjudication work, highlight work priorities, innovate work methods, concentrate efforts on case handling, adhere to overall planning and coordination, strengthen supervision and guidance, and achieve new development and new breakthroughs in intellectual property adjudication work.

In 2009, Chinese judges wrote another new chapter in the judicial protection of intellectual property rights with wisdom and hard work.

**I. Lawfully, Impartially, and Efficiently Adjudicating Intellectual Property Cases, Fully Exerting the Leading Role of Judicial Protection of Intellectual Property Rights**

In 2009, faced with an increase in the number of intellectual property cases, an increase in new types of cases, an increase in major and difficult cases, and increased difficulty in case adjudication, the People's Courts consistently regarded law enforcement and case handling as their primary task, fully exercised the functions of various intellectual property adjudications, protected intellectual property rights in accordance with the law, and adjudicated various types of intellectual property cases impartially and efficiently. The role of adjudication as the main channel for resolving intellectual property disputes has become more prominent. Judicial protection of intellectual property rights has increasingly gained high trust and full recognition from all sectors of society, both domestically and internationally.

**(1) Lawfully and Properly Adjudicating Civil Intellectual Property Cases, Fully Exerting the Leading Role of Civil Adjudication in Protecting Intellectual Property Rights and Stimulating Independent Innovation**

The number of civil intellectual property cases continued its rapid growth trend of many years, with a significant increase, far exceeding the growth rate of other types of civil and commercial cases. In 2009, local courts nationwide newly accepted and concluded 30,626 and 30,509 first-instance civil intellectual property cases respectively, an increase of 25.49% and 29.73% over the previous year. The total amount of subject matter in litigation for newly accepted first-instance cases reached RMB 3.08495 billion (approximately USD 452.25 million). Among them, 4,422 new patent cases were accepted, an increase of 8.54% over the previous year; 6,906 trademark cases, an increase of 10.80%; 15,302 copyright cases, an increase of 39.73%; 747 technology contract cases, an increase of 19.9%; 1,282 unfair competition cases, an increase of 8.19%; and 1,967 other intellectual property cases, an increase of 46.79%. During the year, a total of 1,361 foreign-related first-instance civil intellectual property cases were concluded, an increase of 19.49% over the previous year; a total of 353 first-instance civil intellectual property cases involving Hong Kong, Macao, and Taiwan were concluded, an increase of 56.89% over the previous year. During the year, a total of 5,340 and 5,492 second-instance civil intellectual property cases were newly accepted and concluded, increasing by 12.21% and 16.88% respectively over the previous year; a total of 100 and 107 retrial cases were newly accepted and concluded, decreasing by 1.96% and increasing by 50.7% respectively over the previous year. In addition, from the implementation of the Antitrust Law on August 1, 2008, to the end of 2009, local courts nationwide accepted and concluded a total of 10 and 6 first-instance civil antitrust cases respectively.

In 2009, the Supreme People's Court newly accepted and concluded 243 and 336 civil intellectual property cases (including pending cases). Among them, 176 new retrial applications were accepted, and 263 cases were concluded (including pending cases), effectively fulfilling its duty of supervising and guiding the intellectual property adjudication of courts nationwide.

Among the cases adjudicated by the People's Courts in 2009, there were a number of cases that attracted high social attention, had a wide impact, and even had a significant international influence. Examples include: the Chint v. Schneider "Miniature Circuit Breaker" utility model patent dispute; the Jianghan Petroleum "Roller Bit" trade secret case; the Wuhan Jingyuan "Flue Gas Desulfurization" method patent case; the BMW v. Century BMW well-known trademark case; the "Wu Liangcai" trademark and unfair competition case; the "Lu Brocade" trademark versus generic name dispute; the "Daodao Tong" navigation electronic map copyright case; the Golden Holiday v. Ctrip air ticket reservation unfair competition case; the "Caile" trademark revocation administrative litigation case; the "Tomato Garden" software online piracy case, etc.

The quality and efficiency of case adjudication continuously improved. The first-instance conclusion rate for civil intellectual property cases in local courts nationwide rose from 81.73% in 2008 to 85.04% in 2009. The appeal rate fell from 49.32% in 2008 to 48.82% in 2009. The retrial rate fell from 0.44% in 2008 to 0.33% in 2009 (Note: Original text says 03.3%, likely a typo for 0.33% or 3.3%. Based on context "下降", 0.33% is most logical). The rate of reversal of appealed cases fell from 6.20% in 2008 to 6.00% in 2009. The conclusion rate for civil intellectual property cases of the Supreme People's Court rose from 55.93% in 2008 to 88.64% in 2009, an increase of 32.71 percentage points.

Fully exerted the special role of interim measures in protecting intellectual property rights. In 2009, local courts nationwide accepted a total of 59 applications for pre-litigation injunctions related to intellectual property, with an order support rate of 85.42%; accepted 237 applications for pre-litigation evidence preservation, with an order support rate of 98.72%; accepted 56 applications for pre-litigation property preservation, with an order support rate of 100%. Overall, the People's Courts were relatively proactive in applying interim measures to protect intellectual property rights, with a relatively high rate of order support.

**(2) Severely Punishing Crimes of Infringing Intellectual Property Rights According to Law, Fully Exerting the Function of Criminal Adjudication in Punishing and Deterring Crimes of Infringing Intellectual Property Rights**

People's courts have fully exercised their function of criminal judicial protection of intellectual property rights, lawfully applied various criminal sanctions, intensified efforts to combat IPR infringement crimes, and severely cracked down on all types of IPR criminal activities. In 2009, local courts nationwide concluded a total of 3,660 criminal cases involving IPR infringement, an increase of 10.04% over the previous year; 5,836 persons were subject to effective judgments, an increase of 8.31% over the previous year, of whom 5,832 were convicted, an increase of 8.28% over the previous year. Among the concluded cases, 1,007 were adjudicated as IPR infringement crimes, with 1,605 persons subject to effective judgments, representing a year-on-year increase of 1.1% and a decrease of 3.14%, respectively; 646 cases were adjudicated as crimes of producing and selling counterfeit and substandard goods (involving IPR infringement), with 1,114 persons subject to effective judgments; 1,973 cases were adjudicated as the crime of illegal business operations (involving IPR infringement), with 3,076 persons subject to effective judgments; and 34 cases involving IPR infringement were adjudicated under other crimes, with 41 persons subject to effective judgments. The judgments in some cases had a significant impact both domestically and internationally. For instance, the case of Chengdu Gongruan Network Technology Co., Ltd. v. Sun Xianzhong, Hong Lei, et al. for copyright infringement (the "Tomato Garden" software piracy case), adjudicated by the Huqiu District People's Court of Suzhou, Jiangsu Province, is a successful example of using criminal judicial channels to combat large-scale online software piracy in China. This case dealt a heavy blow to websites and other infringers who sought to obtain illegal profits through piracy, demonstrating China's good image of strictly fulfilling international conventions and providing equal protection to copyright holders both domestically and abroad.

3. Lawfully fulfilling the judicial review function over administrative acts concerning intellectual property, and fully playing the role of supervising and supporting administrative IPR enforcement.

People's courts have effectively exercised their judicial review function over IPR administrative acts through administrative trials, supervising and supporting administrative agencies in lawfully exercising their powers, protecting the lawful rights and interests of private parties in IPR administrative proceedings, maintaining the order of IPR administrative management, and promoting administrative IPR protection. In 2009, local courts nationwide newly received and concluded 2,072 and 1,971 first-instance IPR administrative cases, respectively, representing year-on-year increases of 92.92% and 90.99%. Among these, they newly received 688 patent cases (up 19.03% year-on-year), 1,376 trademark cases (up 184.3% year-on-year), 4 copyright cases (down 42.86% year-on-year), and 4 other cases. The Supreme People's Court newly received and concluded 54 and 56 IPR administrative cases (including pending cases from previous years).

IPR administrative cases primarily consist of grant and confirmation administrative cases where the Patent Reexamination Board of the China National Intellectual Property Administration and the Trademark Review and Adjudication Board of the State Administration for Industry and Commerce are the defendants. In 2009, the growth rate of such administrative cases reached a historic high, significantly increasing the caseload pressure. According to statistics, the Beijing No. 1 Intermediate People's Court newly received and concluded 626 and 594 first-instance patent administrative cases, respectively, representing year-on-year increases of 20.38% and 34.69%; the Beijing High People's Court newly received and concluded 361 and 337 second-instance patent administrative cases, respectively, representing year-on-year increases of 11.42% and 17.01%. The Beijing No. 1 Intermediate People's Court newly received and concluded 1,346 and 1,222 first-instance trademark administrative cases, respectively, representing year-on-year increases of 209.42% and 333.33%; the Beijing High People's Court newly received and concluded 465 and 416 second-instance trademark administrative cases, respectively, representing year-on-year increases of 144.73% and 195.03%.

4. Intensifying mediation efforts in intellectual property cases and striving to build a "grand mediation" pattern for intellectual property adjudication.

While adjudicating cases through judgments, people's courts lawfully utilized the function of mediation, a "Eastern experience," integrating the working principle of "mediation first, combining mediation and adjudication" throughout the entire process of IPR adjudication, focusing on achieving substantive resolution of disputes. In 2009, the level of mediation by people's courts continuously improved, the mediation rate increased, and the effectiveness of IPR litigation mediation was significant. The average rate of mediation and withdrawal for first-instance IPR civil cases in local courts nationwide reached 61.08%, an increase of 5.22 percentage points year-on-year. For example, when the Zhejiang High People's Court heard the appeal in the case of Chint Group v. Schneider Electric regarding the "Miniature Circuit Breaker" utility model patent infringement, it facilitated a global settlement agreement between Schneider Electric (France) and Chint Group, resolving not only the long-standing IPR disputes between the parties in multiple countries but also creating a market environment for benign competition and playing a positive role in improving bilateral relations. In the case of Jianghan Petroleum "Roller Cone Drill Bit" trade secret infringement heard by the Hubei High People's Court, after nearly fifty sessions of patient mediation, the parties finally reached a package mediation agreement covering the instant case and all related disputes. Both parties expressed high satisfaction, achieving excellent social results. During the trial of the "Hao Xiang Ni" (Dear) trademark administrative dispute case, the Supreme People's Court, with the assistance of the Henan High People's Court and in collaboration with relevant local government departments, conducted meticulous mediation efforts, ultimately leading the parties to reach a settlement and withdraw retrial applications for four cases, simultaneously facilitating the resolution of 105 trademark disputes and infringement cases between them. People's courts actively innovated mediation methods, proactively strengthened cooperation with relevant departments, and continuously improved the dispute resolution mechanism connecting litigation and non-litigation methods, fundamentally resolving conflicts and disputes. For instance, on November 3, the Beijing High People's Court, on behalf of the Beijing court system, formally established a mechanism for entrusted mediation of internet dispute cases with the Online Mediation Center of the Internet Society of China, generating a positive social response. Higher people's courts in Zhejiang, Sichuan, Guangxi, and other regions issued guiding opinions on strengthening mediation in IPR civil litigation, achieving good results. The Supreme People's Court focused on conciliation work in cases applying for retrial; when parties reached a settlement, upon their request, it attempted to describe the relevant content of the settlement agreement in the ruling granting the withdrawal of the retrial application and corrected obvious errors in the original judgment.

5. Further implementing the open trial system and continuously increasing the transparency of intellectual property justice.

In 2009, in their IPR adjudication work, people's courts further implemented the constitutional principle of open trials, strictly complied with the provisions on procedure openness in the three major procedural laws, and actively followed the requirements of the Supreme People's Court's "Six Provisions on Judicial Openness," "Several Provisions on People's Courts Accepting Supervision by News Media and Public Opinion," and "Several Opinions on Strengthening the Work of Trial Openness in People's Courts" to expand the scope and channels of judicial openness. They ensured open trials throughout the entire adjudication process, strengthened and standardized the obligation to inform parties according to law, and effectively safeguarded the rights of parties to be informed, participate, express opinions, and supervise at all stages of IPR case filing, trial, enforcement, and trial supervision. They consciously accepted social supervision, protected the lawful rights and interests of parties, and promoted judicial fairness. They fully utilized the role of the "China IPR Adjudication Documents Website" and local court websites as platforms for publishing IPR adjudication documents, improved the management mechanism for document publication, updated information in a timely manner, and intensified efforts to publish IPR adjudication documents online. By the end of 2009, 34,263 effective IPR adjudication documents had been published through the "China IPR Adjudication Documents Website." The Zhejiang High People's Court invited representatives from foreign governments, international organizations' offices in China, and domestic and foreign media to participate in the province's IPR adjudication work conference, further demonstrating the openness and transparency of IPR adjudication.

II. Actively serving the overall situation of economic and social development and deeply implementing the National Intellectual Property Strategy.

The IPR adjudication work of people's courts is closely related to the overall situation of the Party and the State. In 2009, people's courts closely focused on the national strategic decision of "maintaining growth, ensuring people's livelihood, and promoting stability," deeply implemented the National Intellectual Property Strategy, comprehensively strengthened the construction of the judicial protection system for intellectual property, and provided strong judicial guarantees for building an innovative country and comprehensively building a moderately prosperous society.

1. Adopting effective measures to ensure the implementation of the National Intellectual Property Strategy.

Since the 17th National Congress of the Communist Party of China explicitly proposed "implementing the IPR strategy," and the State Council issued the "Outline of the National Intellectual Property Strategy" on June 5, 2008, deciding to implement the National Intellectual Property Strategy, people's courts have attached great importance to its implementation. The Supreme People's Court specifically established a leading group for implementing the National Intellectual Property Strategy and issued the "Task Division for Implementing the Outline of the National Intellectual Property Strategy" by the Supreme People's Court on February 25, 2009, breaking down and assigning 20 specific tasks involving the work of people's courts. On March 23, 2009, the Supreme People's Court issued the "Opinions on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the National Intellectual Property Strategy." This Opinion put forward specific work requirements for people's courts to implement the "Outline of the National Intellectual Property Strategy" from aspects such as fully recognizing the significant meaning of implementing the National IPR Strategy, fully leveraging the leading role of judicial IPR protection, effectively intensifying judicial IPR protection, improving the IPR adjudication system and working mechanism, optimizing the allocation of adjudication resources, strengthening IPR judicial interpretation work, and enhancing the construction of the IPR adjudication team. It has become a programmatic document guiding IPR adjudication work for a period to come, laying the foundation for people's courts to implement the National IPR Strategy. Local courts nationwide, following the deployment and requirements of the Supreme People's Court and combining local actual conditions, actively adopted practical and feasible measures, thereby effectively implementing the National IPR Strategy in the IPR adjudication work of people's courts. Higher people's courts in Tianjin, Hebei, Shanghai, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Anhui, Hunan, Sichuan, Gansu, Qinghai, and other regions all issued guiding documents for implementing the National IPR Strategy.

2. Actively responding to the international financial crisis and leveraging the unique role of IPR judicial protection.

To address the impact of the international financial crisis on China's real economy, in January 2009, the Supreme People's Court held a legal forum on IPR adjudication responding to the financial crisis's impact on the real economy and service outsourcing, discussing specific measures for IPR adjudication work to promote stable and relatively fast economic growth. In April, the Supreme People's Court issued the "Opinions on Several Issues Concerning IPR Adjudication Serving the Overall Situation under the Current Economic Situation." Based on the new requirements and expectations for IPR adjudication under the severe and complex international and domestic economic situation, this Opinion clarified and improved a series of IPR judicial policies under the current economic situation from four aspects: strengthening the targeting and effectiveness of IPR adjudication in serving the overall situation, intensifying patent protection, strengthening commercial标识 protection, and improving the IPR litigation system. Notably, the Opinion unequivocally stated that "under the current economic situation, IPR judicial protection can only be strengthened and enhanced, not weakened or relaxed," promptly responding to and clarifying the societal debate at the time about whether IPR protection should be strengthened in the context of the international financial crisis. This Opinion not only had significant guiding significance for the IPR judicial protection work of people's courts but also actively guided and regulated enterprises and the market, generating significant domestic and international influence and receiving widespread praise from domestic academia, industry, and the international community. Local courts nationwide adopted corresponding measures to actively respond to the international financial crisis. For example, higher people's courts in Jiangsu, Anhui, Guangxi, and other regions issued specific guiding opinions, putting forward concrete requirements for further improving IPR adjudication work to promote local independent innovation. The Zhejiang High People's Court, in conjunction with the Administration for Industry and Commerce, Customs, and other departments, specifically discussed trademark legal issues in foreign-related OEM processing, promoting enterprises' transition from OEM processing to independent innovation. Court systems in Fujian Province strengthened communication and coordination with public security, procuratorial, industrial and commercial, copyright, and other functional departments for IPR protection, promoting the formation of benign interaction and joint protection forces between judicial and administrative enforcement. The Guangdong High People's Court conducted discussions through various channels, delved into industries to understand the situation, and actively explored judicial countermeasures.

3. Improving the IPR adjudication system and working mechanism, and vigorously strengthening the construction of the IPR adjudication system.

—— Clarifying the division of trial work for IPR administrative cases involving patent, trademark, and other grant and confirmation matters. On June 22, 2009, the Supreme People's Court issued the "Provisions on the Division of Trial Work for IPR Administrative Cases Involving Patent, Trademark, and Other Grant and Confirmation Matters," requiring that from July 1, 2009, all first-instance, second-instance, and retrial cases involving grant and confirmation of IPR such as patents, trademarks, integrated circuit layout designs, and new plant varieties be uniformly adjudicated by the relevant intermediate people's courts in Beijing, the Beijing High People's Court, and the IPR Adjudication Division of the Supreme People's Court, ending the history since 2002 where such cases were separately adjudicated by the IPR Adjudication Division and the Administrative Adjudication Division of the relevant courts. This was an important measure for people's courts to optimize the allocation of adjudication resources, resolve disputes timely and effectively, ensure uniform adjudication standards, and leverage the leading role of judicial IPR protection in the context of implementing the National IPR Strategy. The relevant courts in Beijing effectively implemented the requirements of the "Provisions," promptly adjusted their adjudication forces, and made a good start for the unified adjudication of such cases.

—— Promoting pilot projects where the IPR Adjudication Division uniformly accepts IPR civil, administrative, and criminal cases. In accordance with the relevant requirements of the "Outline of the National Intellectual Property Strategy," in 2009, the Supreme People's Court conducted special research on the pilot projects carried out by local people's courts where the IPR Adjudication Division uniformly accepts IPR civil, administrative, and criminal cases (referred to as the "three-in-one" pilot projects). It approved the High People's Court of Jiangsu Province, the court system of Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region, the High People's Court of Henan Province together with the Zhengzhou and Luoyang Intermediate People's Courts under its jurisdiction, and the Heping District People's Court of Tianjin to carry out "three-in-one" pilot projects. By the end of 2009, 5 high people's courts, 44 intermediate people's courts, and 29 basic people's courts nationwide had carried out related pilots. Higher people's courts in pilot regions issued normative documents to regulate and coordinate related pilot work.

—— Adjusting and improving the jurisdictional layout of IPR cases. In May 2009, the Supreme People's Court issued a "Notice on Effectively Adjusting and Improving the Jurisdictional System for IPR Cases," requiring local courts to continue adhering to the system of designated jurisdiction for technology-related cases and strictly control the number of intermediate people's courts newly granted jurisdiction over patent cases, while actively carrying out cross-regional jurisdiction work for intermediate and basic courts based on the principle of convenience for both parties litigating and courts adjudicating. The Supreme People's Court designated the Yiwu City People's Court of Zhejiang Province as a pilot court for hearing first-instance utility model and design patent dispute cases, and designated the Intermediate People's Courts of Harbin, Qiqihar, Yichang, Xiangfan, Xiamen, Quanzhou, Baotou, and the Agricultural Division 12 and Agricultural Division 8 Intermediate People's Courts of the Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps to accept patent dispute cases across regions. The Supreme People's Court attached great importance to the scientific and rational jurisdictional layout of IPR cases and the balanced development of IPR adjudication work across the national court system, focused on leveraging the advantages of intermediate and basic courts being closest to the parties and facilitating litigation, and vigorously strengthened the capacity building for IPR judicial protection in intermediate and basic courts. By the end of 2009, upon designation by the Supreme People's Court, the number of intermediate people's courts with jurisdiction over patent cases, new plant variety cases, integrated circuit layout design cases, and cases involving the recognition of well-known trademarks reached 75, 41, 46, and 41, respectively, and the number of basic people's courts capable of hearing general IPR civil cases reached 92.

4. Carrying out the annual thematic activity of "Optimizing the Judicial Environment for Independent Innovation" in IPR adjudication, and striving to create a judicial environment conducive to independent innovation.

To address the prominent issues affecting and constraining independent innovation in current IPR judicial protection work, intensify judicial IPR protection, further build a judicial environment conducive to encouraging independent innovation, and stimulate the leading and driving role of technological innovation and independent brands in generating emerging industries, creating social demand, and cultivating new economic growth points, on April 9, 2009, the Supreme People's Court issued a "Notice on Launching the Annual Thematic Activity of 'Optimizing the Judicial Environment for Independent Innovation' in IPR Adjudication in Courts Nationwide." It required courts nationwide to adjudicate patent cases effectively to promote technological innovation; properly adjudicate monopoly cases and unfair competition cases to foster a market order conducive to fair competition; effectively adjudicate trademark cases to promote the development of a brand economy; and strengthen trial supervision and work guidance to practically unify the standards for applying the law. Local courts nationwide also actively formulated activity implementation plans, highlighted the characteristics of their local IPR adjudication work, and implemented them in stages. This thematic activity became one of the highlights and key tasks of people's courts in 2009, achieving important progress in deeply implementing the National IPR Strategy and fully leveraging the leading role of judicial IPR protection.

5. Strengthening judicial response for protecting the IPR of the Shanghai World Expo, and consciously fulfilling the duty of judicial IPR protection.

The 2010 Shanghai World Expo was another world-class event hosted by China following the 2008 Beijing Olympic Games. People's courts fully recognized the significance of hosting the Shanghai World Expo, adhered to active justice, improved the level of justice, and provided fair, efficient, and authoritative IPR judicial guarantees for hosting a "successful, splendid, and unforgettable" World Expo. In 2009, the Supreme People's Court attached great importance to the judicial protection of IPR for the World Expo, adopted active measures, and conducted forward-looking research on various IPR legal application issues that might arise concerning the World Expo. The three-level courts in Shanghai, the host city of the World Expo, proactively responded to the demands for IPR judicial protection arising from the World Expo. While legally, properly, and quickly resolving some IPR disputes related to the World Expo, they focused on extending judicial functions to comprehensively serve and guarantee the World Expo. The Pudong New Area People's Court of Shanghai conducted a live webcast of the trial of the first criminal case related to World Expo IPR, legally finding the defendant guilty of the crime of selling counterfeit registered trademark goods, sentencing the defendant entity, Shanghai Changzheng Materials Co., Ltd., to a fine of RMB 180,000 (approximately USD 26,400), and sentencing the defendant Tan Tian to 2 years' imprisonment and a fine of RMB 100,000 (approximately USD 14,700). This judgment effectively demonstrated the strength of people's courts' judicial protection for IPR related to the World Expo.

6. Organizing "IPR Publicity Week" activities to enhance public awareness of IPR protection.

The Supreme People's Court actively carried out activities for the "National Intellectual Property Publicity Week," focusing on the period around World Intellectual Property Day on April 26, and organized courts nationwide to conduct diverse, content-rich, and wide-ranging promotional activities. These included holding press conferences, formulating guiding documents, publishing annual case reports, announcing typical cases, organizing public hearings, and convening seminars. Through these methods, the court comprehensively and from multiple angles showcased the achievements, current status, and future measures of Chinese courts in the judicial protection of intellectual property. Emphasis was placed on using judicial cases — vivid "living law" — to guide the public in raising awareness of IP protection and to foster an IP culture that respects knowledge, advocates innovation, and adheres to honesty and the rule of law. Courts across various regions carried out activities with their own characteristics. For instance, the Tianjin High People's Court held a symposium between judges and writers; the Shandong and Hubei High People's Courts convened IP judicial protection symposiums with participants from all sectors of society; IP judges from the Guizhou, Gansu, and Qinghai High People's Courts, as well as the Xining Intermediate People's Court, took to the streets to conduct public interest consultations on IP issues; the Liaoning High People's Court and the Changsha Intermediate People's Court of Hunan Province broadcast IP case trials online. Major central news media, leading portal websites, and major local news media provided extensive, in-depth, and continuous coverage of the people's courts' activities during "IP Publicity Week."

III. Continuously Strengthening Trial Supervision and Professional Guidance, Striving to Unify Judicial Standards for Intellectual Property

Unifying judicial standards for intellectual property and ensuring consistency in adjudication criteria are fundamental requirements for establishing a fair, efficient, and authoritative judicial protection system for IP. In 2009, the people's courts worked to maintain judicial uniformity in IP by strengthening trial supervision and professional guidance.

(A) Strengthening Judicial Interpretation Work on Intellectual Property to Unify Adjudication Rules

The Supreme People's Court has always emphasized the important role of judicial interpretations in unifying the application of law. In 2009, with the active cooperation and participation of local courts nationwide, work was initiated on drafting judicial interpretations and normative documents concerning issues such as patent infringement adjudication, judicial protection of well-known trademarks, antitrust civil litigation, patent and trademark authorization and confirmation cases, and online copyright case trials. On April 22, the court issued the "Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Civil Disputes Involving the Protection of Well-known Trademarks," further clarifying the conditions, standards, and evidentiary requirements for protecting well-known trademarks. This responded to societal concerns about well-known trademark protection and effectively promoted the healthy development of a brand economy. On December 28, the court issued the "Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Patent Infringement Disputes," which standardized rules for interpreting patent claims and clarified standards for determining patent infringement. This interpretation is of significant guiding importance for ensuring the correct implementation of the amended Patent Law, handling patent infringement case trials, and actively promoting independent innovation. Based on extensive research, the Supreme People's Court drafted the "Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Monopoly Civil Disputes (Initial Draft)" and the "Opinions on Several Issues Concerning the Trial of Administrative Cases on Trademark Authorization and Confirmation (Initial Draft)," and widely and openly solicited opinions from various quarters, laying the groundwork for subsequent revision, improvement, and implementation.

(B) Strengthening Professional Guidance in Intellectual Property Trials to Ensure Correct Implementation of the Law

Higher-level people's courts attached great importance to providing professional trial guidance to lower-level courts. In 2009, the Supreme People's Court and various High People's Courts, through means such as judicial documents, meeting minutes, and adjudication approvals of typical cases, clarified specific judicial principles and standards for IP protection and promptly resolved some prominent issues in trial practice. Particular attention was paid to issuing judicial documents with universal guiding significance. To ensure the correct implementation of the judicial protection system for well-known trademarks and to address problems arising in the judicial recognition of well-known trademarks, on January 5, the Supreme People's Court issued the "Notice on Issues Concerning the Jurisdiction of Civil Disputes Involving the Recognition of Well-known Trademarks," concentrating jurisdiction over such cases with intermediate people's courts in provincial capitals and cities specifically designated in the state plan. This effectively standardized the judicial recognition of well-known trademarks and upheld the good image of judicial IP protection. To ensure the correct implementation of the amended Patent Law, the Supreme People's Court also issued the "Notice on Studying and Implementing the Amended Patent Law," clarifying transitional issues in the application of the old and new Patent Laws. To address issues encountered in local trial practice, local courts also generally focused on timely summarizing trial experience. For example, the Beijing High People's Court summarized and proposed relatively systematic guiding opinions on the trial of design patent cases; the Zhejiang, Hubei, and Yunnan High People's Courts did so for online copyright infringement cases; the Guangdong High People's Court for cases involving infringement of audio-visual copyrights; and the Shanxi and Qinghai High People's Courts for cases involving the recognition of well-known trademarks. Courts in various regions also paid attention to timely communication and coordination on related and similar cases with significant social impact, unifying trial standards for such cases, ensuring consistency in adjudication results, and maintaining judicial authority.

(C) Actively Leveraging the Demonstrative Effect of Typical Intellectual Property Cases and Innovating Trial Guidance Methods

During the period around World Intellectual Property Day on April 26, the Supreme People's Court released the "Top 10 IP Judicial Protection Cases of 2008 in China" and simultaneously announced 50 typical cases, further promoting and highlighting the demonstrative effect and guiding role of typical cases. For the first time, it published the "Supreme People's Court Annual Report on Intellectual Property Cases (2008)," which compiled the adjudication summaries of 23 typical cases selected from the 184 cases concluded by the Supreme People's Court in 2008. This represented the first concentrated display of typical cases tried by the Supreme People's Court itself in its history and was a novel attempt to innovate the trial guidance system. It played a positive role in timely summarizing trial experience, strengthening trial guidance, and promoting the unification and improvement of standards for the application of IP laws. Local courts also generally focused on the collection, compilation, theoretical analysis, and publication of typical judicial cases to guide trial practice. The "Selected IP Adjudication Documents of Shanghai (1994-2008)" (bilingual Chinese-English edition) edited and published by the Shanghai High People's Court received praise both domestically and internationally.

(D) Strengthening Investigation and Research on Intellectual Property Trials to Provide Theoretical Foundation Support

The people's courts persistently adhered to theoretical innovation, continuously enriched IP trial theory, and valued international exchange and learning in the area of judicial IP protection, thereby enhancing the international influence of Chinese courts in this field. In 2009, the people's courts conducted a series of fruitful investigations, yielding rich theoretical results in trial practice and forming many valuable research findings. These findings were translated into guiding documents and working measures. With the strong cooperation of local courts, the Supreme People's Court conducted special investigations on topics such as online copyright, compensation for damages in audio-visual product infringement, and antitrust civil litigation. It organized international seminars on the judicial protection of internet copyrights, workshops on antitrust civil litigation, and international symposiums on the judicial protection of IP. It sent a "Delegation to Study EU Competition Law" to the UK, Belgium, Germany, and Luxembourg. In cooperation with the U.S. Department of Justice and the Federal Trade Commission, it held a "Sino-U.S. Seminar on Antitrust Civil Litigation Issues." It also launched the publication "Developments in Intellectual Property Trials." These research activities further deepened theoretical research on IP trials and effectively promoted the refinement and unification of adjudication standards. On January 8, with the approval of the Supreme People's Court, the China Judicial Protection of Intellectual Property (Suzhou) Research Base was established at the Suzhou Intermediate People's Court in Jiangsu Province, providing foundational support for IP judicial protection research by courts nationwide. The Supreme People's Court actively utilized the theoretical platform of the Intellectual Property Trial Theory Professional Committee under the Trial Theory Research Society of the China Law Society, organizing various seminar activities, and on April 19, established an IP Trial Research Base of this committee at the Shapingba District People's Court of Chongqing. Local courts continuously deepened their understanding of trial patterns and, based on local realities and trial work needs, proactively conducted research on many important topics, achieving encouraging results that provided important theoretical support for trial work. The people's courts also actively participated in legislative and amending activities for IP laws, organizing specialized teams to contribute to the drafting and revision of laws and regulations such as the Trademark Law, the Anti-Unfair Competition Law, the Implementing Regulations of the Patent Law, the Customs Protection of Intellectual Property Regulations, and the Regulations on the Protection of Folklore, endeavoring to provide constructive opinions and suggestions. In recognition of the outstanding contributions of Chinese courts and judges in the judicial protection of IP, two Chinese IP judges were selected by the British magazine "Managing Intellectual Property" as among the "50 Most Influential People in Intellectual Property Worldwide in 2009."

IV. Comprehensively Strengthening the Construction of the Intellectual Property Judge Team, Continuously Improving Judicial IP Capabilities and Standards

Strict, impartial, and civilized IP justice requires a high-quality team of judges. In 2009, the people's courts, using the theme practice activity "People's Judges for the People" as a vehicle, vigorously strengthened the construction of IP trial organizations, professional capacity building, and integrity building, striving to improve the overall quality of the IP judge team and continuously reinforcing the organizational guarantees and talent base for IP trials.

(A) Focusing on Strengthening the Organizational System for Intellectual Property Trials

In 2009, the organizational system for IP trials in Chinese courts became more robust. Intermediate people's courts and above generally established specialized IP trial divisions, paying attention to selecting and cultivating professional IP judges from personnel with legal expertise, good foreign language skills, a background in science or engineering, and some trial experience, thereby further improving the professional composition of the IP trial team. Functional departments such as case filing, criminal trial, administrative trial, and enforcement in courts at all levels generally designated specific collegiate benches or judges to handle the review, trial, and enforcement of IP cases. In 2009, the people's courts focused on strengthening the foundational work at the grassroots level, further allocating and reinforcing trial forces, and effectively addressing the problem of insufficient judges relative to the caseload in some local IP divisions. Based on the characteristics of IP cases, courts in various regions carefully selected and actively recommended experts in relevant fields to serve as people's assessors, leveraging their professional advantages and unique roles in trying special cases. The Tianjin High People's Court specifically issued the "Opinions on Promoting the Participation of People's Assessors in the Trial of Intellectual Property Cases." The Supreme People's Court, along with the High People's Courts of Shanghai, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Guangdong, and Sichuan, as well as the First and Second Intermediate People's Courts of Beijing, continued to conduct personnel exchanges with specialized IP institutions such as the Patent Reexamination Board. Courts in various regions paid attention to utilizing the role of technical experts in resolving IP disputes. The Shanghai High People's Court established a database of technical experts for IP trials.

(B) Vigorously Strengthening Professional Capacity Building in Intellectual Property Trials

The people's courts attached great importance to intensive training for IP judges in professional knowledge and trial skills, purposefully strengthening the cultivation of specialized IP talent. Training was focused on current hot and difficult issues in IP trials, with increased support for the development of IP trials in central and western courts and grassroots courts, promoting the overall improvement of the national level of IP trials. In August 2009, the Supreme People's Court, at the National Judges College, held a national training seminar on new issues in IP trials for more than 240 IP trial personnel from intermediate and grassroots courts. High People's Courts in places such as Beijing, Heilongjiang, Zhejiang, Shandong, Hubei, Hunan, Guangxi, and Chongqing also held similar training sessions.

(C) Attaching High Importance to the Ideological and Political Development of the Intellectual Property Judge Team

In 2009, the people's courts continued to deepen education on the socialist rule of law concept, educating all IP judges to firmly establish the core judicial values of fairness, integrity, service to the people, and to consciously resist the erosion of various decadent thoughts and unhealthy practices. Efforts were made to continuously improve the political quality, professional competence, and professional ethics of IP judges, ensuring impartial and honest justice. Attention was paid to recognizing and publicizing advanced models of judicial fairness and justice for the people, leveraging their inspirational and exemplary role, and striving to cultivate among IP judges good work styles characterized by closeness to, affection for, and service to the people. On November 17, the Supreme People's Court issued the "Decision on Conferring the Title of 'National Trial Business Expert' on 45 Comrades, Including Kong Xiangjun," and six IP judges were awarded this title, fully demonstrating the excellent professional qualities of Chinese IP judges.

Conclusion

Achievements belong to the past; the honors of the past 30 years and of 2009 have been recorded in history.

In 2010, the implementation of the National Intellectual Property Strategy will enter a more critical period. Facing new situations, new tasks, and new challenges, the people's courts will closely focus on ensuring the implementation of the national strategic deployment to accelerate the transformation of the economic development model and maintain stable and relatively fast economic growth. They will always adhere to handling cases and adjudicating as the primary task, further intensify the judicial protection of IP; continue to thoroughly implement the National Intellectual Property Strategy, fully leveraging the leading role of judicial protection in IP; actively promote judicial reforms in the IP field, further improving the IP trial system and working mechanisms, and continuously enhancing the capacity and level of judicial IP protection; further strengthen supervision and guidance in IP trials, and reinforce the construction of the IP judge team, providing more powerful judicial guarantees for IP to support the building of an innovative country and the comprehensive construction of a moderately prosperous society!
